h1: The 6 Best Ultrasonic Cleaner Solutions for Jewelry of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Jewelry Cleaner Solutions: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 ultrasonic jewelry cleaner solutions compared on dilution ratio, yield per bottle and which stones each formula avoids.
summary: Sylvan Hills 32 oz concentrate is the best jewelry solution for most people: a 1:250 mix stretches one bottle across 50+ gallons, it is non-ammoniated, and a polishing cloth ships in the box. iSonic suits households that clean glasses in the same tank, and GemOro is the economical gallon for hobby benches. For a clear 1 to 40 mix, WoldoClean is the straightforward alternative.
intro: Ultrasonic solution is sold as if it were all the same, and the label price is misleading. A 16 oz bottle at a low sticker price can cost more per tank than a 32 oz concentrate that dilutes 1:250. The numbers that decide value are the dilution ratio and the yield, and both appear in small print on the listing instead of the headline.

We ranked six concentrates on the Primea framework, scoring dilution, yield, stone compatibility and extras. The compatibility line matters most: several formulas openly exclude pearls, opals and turquoise, and one is explicitly not a tarnish remover. Matching the chemistry to your jewelry box is the entire purchase.

products.name: Sylvan Hills 32 Oz Ultrasonic Jewelry Cleaner Solution
products.verdict: A 1:250 concentrate that makes 50+ gallons, non-ammoniated, with a polishing cloth included.
products.description:
Mixed at 1:250 with water, this 32 oz bottle yields more than 50 gallons, which at a typical 20 fl oz tank is hundreds of cleanings. The formula is non-ammoniated and free of abrasives, and a free polishing cloth ships in the box.

It wins on cost per tank by a wide margin: the 16 oz Maplefield bottle covers about 95 cycles, and this covers far more. It ranks above iSonic because it is both cheaper per use and non-ammoniated, though iSonic is easier to dose with a capful.

Buy it if you clean regularly and want a bottle that lasts years. The caveat is that 1:250 is a very high dilution, so measure carefully with a small syringe or marked cup, and do not guess.
products.idealFor: Frequent cleaners who want one bottle to last across hundreds of tanks.
products.skipIf: You prefer a premeasured capful dose.

products.name: iSonic Jewelry and Eyeglass Cleaner Solution Concentrate
products.verdict: One capful per use, made in the USA, with a streak-free lens finish.
products.description:
The iSonic concentrate is designed for jewelry, watches and eyeglasses in the same tank, with one capful per use. The formula is non-toxic and biodegradable, made in the USA, and leaves a streak-free finish on lenses.

The capful dose is the draw: no ratio to calculate, no syringe to find. That simplicity is why it ranks above WoldoClean and GemOro for home users. It falls behind Sylvan Hills because per-use cost is higher, and the listing gives no yield figure.

Choose it if glasses and rings share the tub. The caveat is that a capful is a coarse measure, so you will use more than you need in a small tank.
products.idealFor: Households that clean rings, watches and eyeglasses in one tank.
products.skipIf: You want the lowest cost per cleaning.

products.name: GemOro Jewelry Cleaner Solution Concentrate, 1 Gallon
products.verdict: A gallon superconcentrate that dilutes 40:1 for light work and 20:1 for heavy, built for jewelers' benches.
products.description:
GemOro is a 1-gallon superconcentrate with two dilutions: 40:1 for light cleaning and 20:1 for heavy. It removes dirt, grease, buffing compounds, rouge, tripoli and oxides, and is non-toxic and non-flammable.

That list is the point. It ranks third because it is built for bench use after polishing, not for the weekly clean of a worn ring. It is also explicitly not a tarnish remover, so silver that has gone dark will not brighten.

Buy it if you polish, repair or resize jewelry and need an economical gallon. The caveat is the $25 to $50 price and a bottle larger than most home users will finish.
products.idealFor: Hobby jewelers and busy homes that need a strong, economical bench fluid.
products.skipIf: Your main problem is tarnished silver.

products.name: ERRECOM U-Sonic Jewelry Concentrated Cleaner, 17 fl oz
products.verdict: A 1:10 to 1:40 range lets you tune strength by dirt level.
products.description:
ERRECOM's 17 fl oz concentrate dilutes anywhere from 1:10 to 1:40 depending on dirt level and yields up to 5.28 gallons. It is listed as safe on diamonds, gold, silver, platinum and non-porous gems, and it also cleans eyeglasses, dentures, aligners, coins and keys.

That flexible mix range earns the fourth spot: strong when needed, mild when not. Against Sylvan Hills it is far less economical per tank, and the long list of other uses makes the label broader than the jewelry focus of the winners.

Pick it if one bottle needs to cover many items. The caveat is that the wide mix range invites over-strong mixes, so start at the weak end.
products.idealFor: People who clean jewelry, glasses and small items and want to tune the strength.
products.skipIf: You want the cheapest cost per tank.

products.name: WoldoClean Ultrasonic Jewelry Cleaner Concentrate, 25.4 oz
products.verdict: A fixed 1 to 40 mix, ammonia and alcohol free, that makes 8 gallons.
products.description:
WoldoClean mixes at 1 to 40, giving about 8 gallons from the 25.4 fl oz bottle. The formula is ammonia free and alcohol free, and the listing is clear that it is not for pearls, opals or turquoise. It suits tanks from 8 to 64 fl oz.

It ranks fifth because the yield is middling: Sylvan Hills stretches a similar bottle several times further. The fixed ratio is a plus for people who dislike guessing. The explicit exclusions are the most useful safety information in this entire category.

Good for gold, platinum and diamond pieces. Keep porous stones out, as the label itself says.
pros: Works in 8 to 64 fl oz tanks
products.idealFor: Owners of gold, platinum and diamond pieces who want a clear 1 to 40 mix.
products.skipIf: Your collection includes pearls, opals or turquoise.

products.name: Maplefield Ultrasonic Jewelry Cleaner Solution, 16 oz
products.verdict: Half a capful per 20 fl oz basin and up to 95 cycles per bottle.
products.description:
The Maplefield dose is half a capful per 20 fl oz basin, for up to 95 cleaning cycles from the 16 oz bottle. The listing says it is safe on gold, silver and gemstones and compatible with any ultrasonic cleaner.

The countable dose is the selling point, and the smallest bottle is the reason it ranks last. A buyer with a standard 20 fl oz tank, like the Magnasonic or onlikin, can count exactly how many cleanings remain. But the stone-safe claim is broader and less specific than WoldoClean's explicit exclusions.

Buy it for a home tub with a 20 fl oz basin. Verify any porous stones yourself before use.

whatMatters.detail: The ratio tells you how far a bottle goes. Sylvan Hills at 1:250 stretches a 32 oz bottle across 50+ gallons, while WoldoClean at 1 to 40 yields 8 gallons from 25.4 oz. Compare yield per bottle on the listing, since sticker price alone misleads.

Pearls, opals and turquoise are porous or soft and can be harmed by ultrasonic cleaning and by solutions. WoldoClean names them as excluded. Read the exclusion line before buying, and when in doubt about a stone, leave it out of the tank altogether, because no concentrate can make a fragile stone safe in a vibrating bath.

Ammonia cleans well but can damage some stones, soft metals and finishes. Sylvan Hills is non-ammoniated and WoldoClean is ammonia free. If your listing does not state it, assume it may contain ammonia and avoid it for treated or porous gems, and rinse every piece in clean water afterward.

Some formulas remove oils and light dirt, others strip buffing compounds and oxides. GemOro lists rouge, tripoli and oxides, but is not a tarnish remover. Match scope to the problem: everyday skin oil needs less than post-polish residue, and a stronger mix is not automatically a better one.

A capful is easy but coarse, a ratio is exact but needs a measuring cup. iSonic uses a capful, Maplefield half a capful per 20 fl oz, ERRECOM a 1:10 to 1:40 range. Pick the method you will follow every time, because over-concentration wastes bottle and risks surfaces.

faq.q: Can I use these in any ultrasonic cleaner?
faq.a: Maplefield states compatibility with any ultrasonic cleaner, and the others are formulated for the same use. Check your machine's manual for restrictions, and avoid hot solution in small plastic-housed units unless the maker allows heating.

faq.q: What mistake do people make with concentrate?
faq.a: Mixing it stronger than the label says. A bottle of Sylvan Hills at 1:250 or WoldoClean at 1 to 40 is built to dilute heavily, and extra concentrate does not clean better, it only shortens how long the bottle lasts.

faq.q: Is GemOro worth it over Sylvan Hills?
faq.a: Only if you polish or repair jewelry. GemOro removes buffing compounds, rouge and oxides at 20:1, which routine cleaning does not need. For rings that just carry skin oil, Sylvan Hills 32 oz is cheaper per tank.

faq.q: How do I set up a tank?
faq.a: Mix the solution in the tank at the stated ratio, such as one capful of iSonic or half a capful of Maplefield per 20 fl oz, then run a short degas before adding jewelry. Rinse pieces in clean water afterward.

faq.q: How long does mixed solution keep?
faq.a: Mixed solution turns cloudy as it fills with oils, and can be reused briefly if clear. For ERRECOM or WoldoClean, discard when it clouds. Do not store mixed solution in a closed bottle, since it turns stale and smells.

faq.q: Do any of these remove tarnish?
faq.a: Not reliably. GemOro states it is not a tarnish remover, and the others focus on dirt and oils. For silver tarnish use a dedicated tarnish remover or polishing cloth, such as the free cloth included with Sylvan Hills.

finalTake: Sylvan Hills 32 Oz Ultrasonic Jewelry Cleaner Solution is the best buy for most people because the 1:250 mix delivers 50+ gallons from one bottle and the non-ammoniated formula is gentler on stones. iSonic is the easy household pick, GemOro serves benches, and WoldoClean is the clearest on what to avoid. Always read the stone exclusions before you pour.
